items.followUp: Name two pigments that assist chlorophyll in absorbing light.

rubric.why: Accessory pigments include chlorophyll b and carotenoids such as carotenes and xanthophylls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct accessory pigment.

rubric.why: Two distinct accessory pigments are required.
rubric.description: Names a second, different accessory pigment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct name distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Two accessory pigments are chlorophyll b and carotenoids.

items.followUp: Name two pigments other than chlorophyll a that absorb light in plants.

rubric.why: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration generally raises the rate of photosynthesis when other conditions are suitable.
rubric.description: States that increasing carbon dioxide increases the rate of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct initial effect.

rubric.why: The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting or the carbon dioxide concentration reaches saturation.
rubric.description: States that the rate eventually levels off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the limiting or saturation effect.

modelAnswer: As carbon dioxide concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases if other conditions are suitable.
At a certain concentration, the rate levels off because another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: Give one difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration and state one product of each.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration takes place without oxygen.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the processes by oxygen requirement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the presence or absence of oxygen.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water; anaerobic respiration can produce lactic acid in muscles or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.
rubric.description: Gives correct products of the two processes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the aerobic products and a correct anaerobic product or products.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water.
Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen; it produces lactic acid in muscles, or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.

items.followUp: List the main organs of the human alimentary canal in order.

rubric.why: The canal begins with the mouth and continues through the pharynx and oesophagus to the stomach.
rubric.description: Names the mouth-to-stomach parts of the canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct sequence, allowing omission of the pharynx.

rubric.why: After the stomach, food passes through the small and large intestines, then the rectum and anus.
rubric.description: Names the intestinal and terminal parts of the canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct sequence, allowing omission of the rectum.

modelAnswer: The alimentary canal consists of the mouth, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum and anus.

items.followUp: Write two common symptoms of a peptic ulcer.

rubric.why: Abdominal or stomach pain, often with a burning sensation, is a common ulcer symptom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct pain symptom.

rubric.why: Nausea, vomiting, indigestion and loss of appetite can occur with ulcers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one additional correct symptom.

modelAnswer: Common symptoms of an ulcer include pain or a burning sensation in the stomach.
Other symptoms may include nausea, vomiting or indigestion.

items.followUp: State two dietary or lifestyle factors that can cause constipation.

rubric.why: A diet lacking fibre or roughage can cause constipation.
rubric.description: Identifies insufficient dietary fibre or roughage.

rubric.why: Insufficient water, inactivity or ignoring the urge to defecate can contribute to constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one additional correct cause.

modelAnswer: Constipation may be caused by eating too little fibre or roughage.
It may also result from drinking too little water, lack of exercise or ignoring the urge to defecate.

items.followUp: What are vitamins? Name the water-soluble vitamins.

rubric.why: Vitamins are organic substances needed in small amounts for normal growth and proper body functioning.
rubric.description: Defines vitamins as organic substances needed in small amounts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential definition.

rubric.why: The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E and K.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete set.

modelAnswer: Vitamins are organic substances required in small amounts for normal growth and proper functioning of the body.
The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E and K.

items.followUp: State one function of red blood cells and one function of white blood cells.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body by fighting infection and destroying pathogens.
rubric.description: States the function of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct defence function.

rubric.why: Platelets help the blood to clot and stop bleeding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct clotting function.

modelAnswer: White blood cells defend the body against infection and pathogens.
Platelets help the blood to clot and stop bleeding.
